intent: Lay out several attachments in one horizontally scrolling, snapping row.
typical_uses: The files attached to one message or waiting in a composer

dont_use_when.situation: Attachments that should wrap onto several lines or stack in a column

instead.target: a plain flex or grid container in the consuming application
instead.note: AttachmentGroup always lays its children out in one row that scrolls horizontally; the kit ships no wrapping attachment layout.

dont_use_when.situation: Images or slides the user steps through one viewport at a time

invariants.text: The group is a flex row that scrolls horizontally with mandatory snapping and spaces its children var(--space-3) apart; each direct Attachment child keeps its own width and snaps to its start edge.
The group adds the global `scroll-fade-x` and `no-scrollbar` classes; the edge fade and the hidden scrollbar draw only when the package's utilities.css is loaded.
The group renders a div with no role and no tab stop of its own, so a row of attachments with no trigger or actions cannot be scrolled from the keyboard unless the caller makes the group focusable.

good.title: Two small attachments in a row

bad.title: A size set on the group
bad.why: AttachmentGroup declares no `size` and its div surface has none, so TypeScript rejects it; the size belongs on each Attachment.
